text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#78901 - metrics-pipeline: prom-scrape-throttle. Priority: P1. Acknowledgement window: 5m. Link: https://pd.example/incident/78901

maria: saw it. prometheus scrape failures spiking, exporter 10.0.12.34 returning 503s, lots of 504s in scrape logs.

jen: acked in PD. I'm joining. Any customer-facing alerts?

akshay: not surfaced to customers yet, but synthetic checks show increased latency for embeddings route. Could be downstream log-ingest backlog.

maria: quick check: prometheus logs show repeated `context deadline exceeded` from the scrape proxy. Also seeing kafka consumer lag in ingest-consumer (~240k messages).

ops-bot: autoscale event: metrics-ingest-consumer increased replicas from 3 -> 6 (reason: consumer lag high).

carol: @maria can you paste the exporter logs? want to confirm timeout vs OOM.

maria: pasting tail of exporter stderr: ```
2026-02-15T12:04:01Z exporter: GET /metrics -> 503 service unavailable
2026-02-15T12:04:03Z exporter: Read timeout after 30s
2026-02-15T12:04:05Z exporter: connection reset by peer
```

jen: hmm. kubelet reports 0 OOMs on that node. CPU is spiking on the exporter pod (95%). Could be GC thrashing after a bad config.

akshay: rolling restart of exporter daemonset on cluster-prod-1 to eliminate stateful leak? that may cause short scrape gap.

maria: agree. plan: 1) scale exporter CPU to 2x on the problematic node pool 2) restart exporter pods one at a time 3) monitor prometheus scrape success rate and kafka lag.

jen: I'm going to run the patch now. will keep PD updated.

jen: running command: ```sh
kubectl -n monitoring set resources deployment/exporter --limits=cpu=1000m,memory=512Mi --requests=cpu=500m,memory=256Mi
kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deployment/exporter
```

maria: copying prometheus scrape status query: `sum by(job,instance)(increase(prometheus_scrape_duration_seconds_count[5m]))` - scrape times jumped from ~0.2s -> 35s around 12:03 UTC.

ops-bot: metric alert recovered: prom-scrape-duration returned to baseline.

jen: first pod restarted cleanly. second pod shows restart count 3, digging. Getting a stacktrace: `goroutine 1273: runtime: out of memory` in the container logs for exporter-2.

akshay: that explains the CPU/GC. if it's OOMing we should cordon that node and evict to avoid thrash. I'll scale a temporary replica set and cordon node-57.

carol: customer-impact note: embeddings route latency elevated ~200ms for 10% of requests between 12:02-12:09 UTC. No error rate increase observed. tagging customers who run low-latency SLAs.

jen: cordoning node-57 and draining pods now:
```sh
kubectl cordon node-57
kubectl drain node-57 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

maria: after the drain, exporter pods rescheduled to node-61 and node-62. prometheus scrape success back to 99.9% in the last 2m. kafka lag starting to drop (now 45k).

akshay: continuing to monitor consumer lag. if it stalls above 100k we'll add a consumer instance.

jen: PD note: ack remains, auto-escalation suppressed. I've added the remediation steps to the incident timeline.

maria: follow-up: we'll open a ticket to investigate exporter memory leak (likely new release). tagging eng-runtime to triage.

carol: logged customer impact + timeline. will loop in account teams for the affected customers.

ops-bot: autoscale: metrics-ingest-consumer scaled up to 8 replicas at 12:12 UTC.

jen: kafka lag down to 12k, prometheus scrape stable, exporter pod memory now steady ~300Mi. I'm going to resolve PD after two clean minutes.

maria: +1 from me. recommend bumping exporter memory request to avoid future OOMs permanently in a follow-up change.

jen: resolving PD#78901 (mitigation complete, follow-up ticket created: INF-4521). :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident closed by jen. Duration: 00:12:20. Summary: exporter OOMs on node-57 caused prom-scrape timeouts and subsequent kafka consumer lag; hotfix: restart + drain node + scale consumers. Follow-up: memory leak triage (ENG-RUNTIME) and permanent resource bump.
